docs.title: BLV 3D Printers
docs.text:
Open-source 3D printers by Ben Levi. An archive of the BLV mgn Cube, BLV Ender 3 Pro and BLV mgn12 projects.

I design open-source 3D printers, and the BLV projects are my way of thanking the 3D printing community. This site has the guides, assembly videos, BOMs, sketches and original CAD files needed to build a BLV printer. The projects are non-profit and free for non-commercial use.

Sincerely yours,Ben Levi

docs.title: About me
docs.text:
Design with your heart, make with your mind, and share with those who taught you.

I'm Ben Levi, the developer behind the BLV open-source 3D printers. I learned most of what I know about 3D printing from the early community forums, where every comment and thread was valuable and laid the foundations for what we all use today.

Each BLV project took more than 300 hours of design, testing and documentation. I did it alongside a day job that has nothing to do with 3D printing, a wife and two young children. It wasn't easy, but this work became a kind of therapy for me and brought back a passion I thought I had lost.

Sharing is the reason the projects exist. When the FDM patent expired, open sharing of knowledge is what turned 3D printing into what it is now. If everyone had kept their findings to themselves, none of it would exist. The BLV projects are my way of giving back, so they are free for non-commercial use, with all the files, guides and CAD sources included.

The projects are no longer updated, and this site keeps them available as an archive.

Sincerely yours,Ben Levi

docs.title: BLV Ender 3 Pro
docs.text:
Upgrade mod

The BLV Ender 3 Pro is an upgrade project for the popular Ender 3 Pro 3D printer. It replaces the printed and wheel-based parts with all-aluminum parts, MGN12 linear rails and a BMG dual drive extruder, for better accuracy, efficiency and print quality.

Download all files Thingiverse Remixes Facebook group

Kits are no longer sold

The ready-made BLV Ender 3 Pro aluminum kits are no longer available. The drawings and files are still here, so the parts can be made by a CNC service for personal use.

BLV Ender 3 ProBLV Ender 3 Pro print sample

docs.title: Why build it
docs.text: Fast, reliable, accurate Low and mid range printers usually move on linear bearings or Delrin wheels because they are cheap, and the price is accuracy and reliability. MGN linear rails are stiffer, more precise and smoother, so prints are faster without losing quality. That is why high-end printers use them. If you are tired of worn POM wheels that need constant tightening, this upgrade is for you. Rigid parts This project takes a different path from the earlier ones. Printed parts flex a little, so CNC machined aluminum parts replace them. To test the difference I logged a dial indicator to a database on my PC. After more than 2000 measuring loops of uniformity and deviation, the aluminum parts gave clearly better results than printed parts. Accessible CNC parts are usually expensive. To keep the cost down, the design was offered free for commercial use with my permission. Design time (more than 200 hours here) is a large part of the price of such parts, so manufacturers could sell the kit for less. While it was on sale, 4 aluminum parts typically sold for $30 or more on AliExpress, and this kit had 16 pieces for $59, including belts, screws and shipping. Other aluminum and rail kits cost $300 or more. Open source Why give the work away? I learned everything I know about 3D printing from this community, and the BLV projects are my way of giving back. The same idea is behind the BLV mgn Cube and the BLV Anet mod. When the FDM patent expired, open sharing of knowledge is what built everything we have now. Imagine if everyone had kept their findings to themselves.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
1. Prepare. Read the project description, watch the 3D animation videos and make sure you understand the structure.
  2. Get the parts. Order everything in the BOM, plus spare T-nuts and screws, and prepare the tools.
  3. Build. A precise frame is the basis of good prints, and several YouTube videos show how to align the Ender 3 Pro frame. Use the printed jigs when installing the MGN rails, they make the assembly much easier. Take your time fixing the rails to the extrusions. This short video by 3D Distributed shows an easy way to align parallel rails.

  4. Install the electronics. For the SKR Mini E3 V1.2 board there is a good YouTube installation guide. The Duet WiFi 1.04 board is also an option.

    SKR Mini E3 installation guide

  5. Software, tests and calibration. This step needs some experience, or one of the many YouTube guides on calibrating the Ender 3 Pro. I recommend replacing the original firmware with a fresh Marlin build. Don't skip:

    • Wiring and endstop check
    • Firmware update (fresh Marlin)
    • Extruder calibration
    • Feed rate calibration
    • Hotend PID
    • Bed PID
    • Probe Z offset or Z offset
  6. Print and maintain. Grease the rails with white lithium grease or light sewing machine oil. Keep the rails clean and the belts tight. Clean the PEI plate with alcohol after every print, and lightly scuff new sheets with brass wool.
  7. Share your build. Post an "I made one" photo. Knowing the project helped you makes all the hours worth it.
  8. Remix and share. The source file is included so you can improve the design. Please share your remixes with the community.
  9. Commercial use. Read the legal license first.

docs.title: Hotend
docs.text:
A better hotend is a recommended upgrade. First decide between Bowden and direct drive.

BowdenDirect drive
  • The original Creality hotend | cheap hotend clone
  • High quality hotend by Mellow
  • Excellent quality hotend by Trianglelab
  • Dragon V2 hotend, excellent results

Trianglelab DDE direct drive, 24V full set, a great system.

Its X carriage is very similar to the original Ender carriage. To install the DDE, drill two small holes for M3×6 mm screws in the carriage. It takes about 2 minutes (how).

Use the two screws for alignment only, then remove them.

docs.title: Z axis
docs.text:
Choose a Z setup:

  1. Single Z stepper. It worked well for me for a while, but dual Z adds rigidity and greatly improves the Z axis.
  2. Dual Z with one stepper. A dual Z set with one stepper, 2 threaded rods and a belt. This BMG bracket recovers some of the lost Z height. Some height is still lost because the extruder touches the left top plate, but this became my favorite setup. Replace the Phillips screws that come with the set with hex socket head screws.
  3. Dual Z with two steppers. The recommended set for dual Z with a second Z motor. Align the Z axis so both sides match.

Note

This method reduces the Z height, since the BMG can touch the top plates.

docs.text: The original Creality belt is too flexible and reduces print quality. Use a fiberglass-reinforced GT2 6 mm belt instead. The X axis belt is clamped at a length of 785 mm, measured between the clamps and not including the brass clamps. When replacing a belt, both ends can be locked with a zip tie.

The dual Z option requires moving the PSU:

  1. Disconnect the PSU from the wall.
  2. Disconnect the PSU from the printer.
  3. Partly remove the plastic cover from the PSU.
  4. Drill M5 holes as shown below.

docs.title: Smart filament sensor
docs.text:
Why pay $15 for the SKR smart filament sensor when a wire and an endstop switch cost $1.5? This video explains the difference.

A switch sensor only detects whether filament is present. If the spool jams or the filament gets stuck, nothing happens and the printer keeps printing air. The smart sensor tracks filament movement with a rotary encoder and pauses the print when the filament stops moving. It is well worth it, especially for long prints of 12 hours or more.

docs.title: PEI surface
docs.text: After a long time with the Energetic PEI spring steel sheet, I tested the Trianglelab double-coated PEI sheet. It arrived well packed, with alcohol wipes and a printed manual. On the first try the corners lifted. The last tip in the manual solved it: scuff the PEI well with brass wool, and prints stick very well. Unlike the Energetic sheet, prints also release easily once the sheet cools down.

docs.title: LED installation
docs.text:
Use a 5V, 60 LEDs/m, non-waterproof strip that can be cut after every LED. The non-waterproof type slides into the V-slot channel more easily.

  1. Cut a 15-LED strip, solder a long 4-wire cable to it, and slide it into the top V-slot channel.
  2. Cut a 3-LED strip, solder a cable to it, and secure it with 2 zip ties to the back of the transparent BMG extruder.
  3. Connect both strips together and check the connection.
  4. Then either:
    • connect them to a simple RGB LED controller and use the IR remote, or
    • connect them to the SKR Mini E3 LED pins and configure it.

docs.title: Rail tips
docs.text:
I started with affordable MGN12H rails from AliExpress at about $18 each. After buying from four different sellers, I found the best value at the CNA Mechanical Parts Store. Their carriages slide smoothly straight out of the box, with no cleaning needed. For higher quality at a reasonable price, the HIWIN rail set is excellent.

Sellers to avoid

Avoid RDC Official Store and linkcnc Store on AliExpress. linkcnc sent me a used, damaged rail that was shorter than ordered and stayed stuck even after cleaning. RDC started shipping carriages that don't match the MGN standard.

Cleaning and lubrication. New rails usually feel rough because they are coated with a protective oil at the factory. Clean it off (several YouTube videos show how to clean the carriage with WD-40), then lubricate the rails and carriages with sewing machine oil or a PTFE silicone grease. These are miniature rails, so avoid thick grease. The goal is a smooth carriage without free play.

The video below shows the cleaning process well. Work over a container so you don't lose any steel balls. After reassembly there is room for one more ball, which is normal.

Tuning up cheap Chinese linear bearings

Mounting the rails takes patience. They must be perfectly straight and aligned, and rushing this step causes problems later.

Don't rely on the gravity test

Tilting a rail and watching the carriage slide down says nothing about its quality. A rail with too much free play passes easily and then fails every print quality test. The tolerance grade of the rail sets the friction of the carriage.

docs.title: BLV mgn Cube
docs.text:
Open-source 3D printer

The BLV mgn Cube is an open front CoreXY 3D printer that runs on MGN linear rails. It was designed for accuracy, efficiency and print quality, with one simple goal: to let anyone build a good and reliable 3D printer.

1.78Mdownloads6.3Mviews29/10/22last update

Start building Download the files

BLV mgn Cube at 9000 mm/s² acceleration and 500 mm/s

docs.title: Why build it
docs.text: Fast, reliable, accurate Most low and mid range printers move on linear bearings or Delrin wheels because they are cheap. The price is accuracy and reliability. MGN linear rails are stiffer, more precise and much smoother, so you can print faster without losing quality. That is why high-end printers use them. When I found affordable MGN rails on AliExpress, I decided to build around them. Rigid open structure The open front is as rigid as a closed cube but still gives easy access to the bed and the prints. A front belt tensioner makes maintenance easier. The design came out of many hours of simulation and physical stress tests. Accessible Every part is easy to source, print or make. The BOM has no expensive or rare machined parts. Most parts are printed or bought online or locally. You can also use your own electronics, as long as you know how to adapt the firmware. Open source The original CAD files (STEP) are included in the project files. You are welcome to modify, remix and improve them. If you do, please share your work with the community, mark the parts as "remixed" and link back to this project. Ready to print I spent many hours tuning the firmware and the Simplify3D slicing profile for this printer. After the build, upload the config files, load the profile and start printing. Modular Both the Z height and the bed size can grow. You only need longer extrusions and rails. The included CAD file helps you calculate the dimensions of a custom size. Easy to build? Installing the rails takes about 70% of the build time. It takes precision and a few hours of alignment, and it is worth every minute when the printer runs. To help, the project includes 3D animation videos, PDF guides, sketches and measurements. Balanced budget The BOM aims for the best value without cutting quality: a top 32-bit board, good stepper motors and reliable sensors. A 5" PanelDue touch screen is optional. You can save $80 and use a phone or tablet instead with no loss of features.

docs.title: Reinforcement for taller Z builds
docs.text: For a printer taller than standard, add a 496 mm reinforcing extrusion at the top, just below the front tensioners, as in the picture. It keeps the frame stable at any height.

docs.title: Air scrubbers, HEPA and activated carbon
docs.text:
The project includes a small and a large air scrubber. Printing releases fine particles into the air, and the scrubbers filter them.

Mount the fan so it pushes the air into the filter. The air should pass through the activated carbon first and then through the HEPA filter. Check the filters monthly and replace them when needed.

docs.title: Magnetic heated bed
docs.text:
The best bed is an aluminum MIC6 plate with an AC silicone heater, but it has two drawbacks:

  1. Cost. Both the MIC6 plate and the silicone heater are relatively expensive.
  2. Risk of electric shock if it is not installed correctly.

A 24V bed heats more slowly than an AC bed but is safe to use. The FYSETC parts set came with a magnetic aluminum bed and a BuildTak-like glass surface, which is flat and easy to handle. The original Blurolls set came with a PCB bed, which I recommend less because it tends to warp at high temperatures.

These pictures show the FYSETC bed (see my FYSETC unboxing). The bed parts are also listed in the BOM. Install the magnetic surface layers in exactly the order shown.

docs.title: Internal lighting with a COB LED strip
docs.text:
After a long time with a regular LED strip, I wanted lighting that is hidden, needs no printed parts and shines evenly instead of in spots. The answer was a COB LED strip.

A COB strip has much smaller diodes, about 360 per meter instead of 60, so the light is even. A silicone layer over the diodes works as a diffuser. The strip is also narrow. The 8 mm version slides straight into the extrusion channel. It can be cut every 50 mm and the brightness can be controlled.

The first two strips I ordered from different AliExpress stores were disappointing. Then I found a reliable store with good COB strips. My choice was 6000K cool white, 24V, 360 LEDs per meter, 2 meters.

  1. Cut the strip at the marks (every 50 mm) with scissors.
  2. Solder two 26AWG wires, or use this quick connector (choose "For 8 mm PCB") if you prefer not to solder.
  3. Slide the strip into the upper extrusion channels.
  4. Connect the wires in one of two ways:
    • Directly to a 24V PSU
    • To a Duet fan output, which lets you set the brightness with a slider in the Duet control panel

I use the Duet 3 6HC board from FYSETC, so I defined the lights as a fan output with this line in config.g and connected the strip to the OUT9 port:

M950 F2 C"out9" Q500 M106 P2 S0.2 H-1 C"Lights"

The result is efficient, good-looking light with adjustable brightness from the panel.

docs.title: Linear rail tips
docs.text:
I started with affordable MGN12H rails from AliExpress at about $18 each. After buying from four different sellers, I found the best value at the CNA Mechanical Parts Store. Their carriages slide smoothly straight out of the box, with no cleaning needed. For higher quality at a reasonable price, the HIWIN rail set is excellent.

Sellers to avoid

Avoid RDC Official Store and linkcnc Store on AliExpress. linkcnc sent me a used, damaged rail that was shorter than ordered and stayed stuck even after cleaning. RDC started shipping carriages that don't match the MGN standard.

Cleaning and lubrication. New rails usually feel rough because they are coated with a protective oil at the factory. Clean it off (several YouTube videos show how to clean the carriage with WD-40), then lubricate the rails and carriages with sewing machine oil or a PTFE silicone grease. These are miniature rails, so avoid thick grease. The goal is a smooth carriage without free play.

The video below shows the cleaning process well. Work over a container so you don't lose any steel balls. After reassembly there is room for one more ball, which is normal.

Tuning up cheap Chinese linear bearings

Mounting the rails takes patience. They must be perfectly straight and aligned, and rushing this step causes problems later.

Don't rely on the gravity test

Tilting a rail and watching the carriage slide down says nothing about its quality. A rail with too much free play passes easily and then fails every print quality test. The tolerance grade of the rail sets the friction of the carriage.

docs.title: Calibrations
docs.text:
Before calibrating, make sure the Duet board runs the right firmware. The project was released on RepRap 2.x and later moved to the Duet 3 board with RepRap 3.x. Community member David Husolo published well-tuned BLV Cube configuration files on GitHub for both the Duet 2 WiFi and the Duet 3 running RepRap 3.x.

Several steps below point to the official Duet guides, which cover calibration in detail.

docs.title: 1. Update the Duet firmware
docs.text:
Duet boards are very well documented, with step-by-step guides for almost every task. Update to the latest RepRap firmware 3.x before calibrating. The Duet 2 WiFi and the Duet 3 use the same update guide.

Download the firmware Update guide

docs.title: 2. Copy the config files
docs.text:
Copy the BLV configuration files to the SD card. If the card is new or empty, prepare it first as described in the Duet documentation.

Your setup Config files RepRap 3.x (recommended) David Husolo's GitHub, "firmware" folder. Thank you David! FYSETC parts set FYSETC firmware for the BLV mgn Cube RepRap 2.x The SD card ZIP in the project files. One ZIP is a basic Duet 3 configuration, the other is for RepRap 2.x only.

docs.title: 3. Connect to the web interface
docs.text:
The Duet has a built-in web interface with full control of the printer. This guide explains the network setup:

Network setup guide

Avoid damaging the hardware

  • Never disconnect cables from a powered Duet, except the USB cable.
  • Check all wires for shorts, especially fan, motor and heater wires.
  • Don't feed the board more than 24 volts.
  • Ground the frame and the bed carriage, and the motors if possible.
  • Don't scratch, short or damage the electronics while installing them.
  • Don't remove the memory card while the printer is running.
  • Take your time crimping connectors and check the wires with a multimeter.
  • Triple check the polarity and position of every connection.
  • With the steppers connected, don't move an axis quickly by hand.

docs.title: 4. Configure your printer
docs.text:
The provided configuration covers almost everything. You may still want to center the bed, set motor directions, add macro buttons or define temperature presets per filament. The Duet guides cover all of this:

  • Duet documentation, for both the Duet 2 WiFi and the Duet 3
  • RepRap 3 overview, essential reading

Complete these before moving on:

  • Center your bed
  • Test your endstop switches
  • Set up a different Z probe, only for other probe types
  • Set up a PT100 sensor, only with a PT100

docs.text:
With the FYSETC parts set you can skip this, since its labeled cables match the FYSETC configuration. With steppers from the BOM or the Blurolls set, the motors will probably turn the wrong way at first. Set them up like this:

  1. Identify the coil pairs. A stepper has 4 wires, 2 per coil. This short guide and this video show how to find them.
  2. Connect the steppers using the original Duet stepper wiring, shown in the bottom right corner of wiring diagram v3.2 under "Duet original steppers wiring".
  3. Test and configure them with the Duet documentation. The video shows the expected movement for each test command.
Easily identify the leads of a 4-wire stepper motor with a multimeterBLV mgn Cube 3D printer - steppers test

Then check the directions. In this video I press the jog buttons, and your printer should move the same way.

BLV mgn Cube 3D printer - axis movement

More guides:

  • Tuning stepper motor drivers for the Duet's TMC2660 drivers
  • Mesh bed compensation to change the mesh settings
  • Multiple independent Z motors for true auto leveling
  • Filament sensor

docs.title: 5. Calibrate
docs.text: These calibrations are mandatory. Follow the pictures exactly and work accurately, since they have a large effect on print quality.

docs.title: Hotend PID
docs.text:
The picture shows the classic hotend PID tuning. Newer RepRap 3.x releases add an algorithm that detects fan speed changes and adjusts the heater in advance. To use it:

  • Run the latest 3.x release.
  • Define all your tools (T0) correctly.
  • Define your fans according to the RRF instructions.
  • Turn off the part cooling fan and run M303 T0 S200, with 200 replaced by your usual printing temperature. The algorithm turns the fan on by itself during tuning.

In short, replace M303 H1 S190 with M303 T0 S190.

docs.text:
Read each guide before enabling the feature:

  • Stall detection and sensorless homing
  • Pressure advance to compensate for filament and extruder elasticity
  • Resume a print after a power failure
  • Accelerometer (experimental) to measure ringing frequencies for DAA

docs.title: 3D printing the parts
docs.text: How you print the parts has a large effect on how well they work. Orientation, wall count, filament type and even print speed all matter. Most parts print without supports.

docs.title: Filament
docs.text:
The parts carry loads and work near heat, so choose a strong filament.

Filament Notes PETG What I used PETG Carbon Very rigid, requires a hardened steel nozzle ABS Requires an enclosure, releases toxic fumes PA12 MJF / SLS printed

Don't use PLA or PLA+

The heat inside the printer deforms PLA parts.

docs.title: The build, step by step
docs.text:
1. Prepare. Read the project description and the linked material, watch the 3D animations and explore the printer in the 3D viewer. Make sure you understand the structure before you start.

  2. Get the parts. Waiting for parts is the most frustrating stage. Check that you have everything in the BOM, plus spare T-nuts and screws. If you use your own electronics, make sure you know how to configure the firmware for your board.

  3. Build. Prepare the tools and use a good corner alignment tool. A precise frame is the basis of good prints. The printed jigs make the assembly much easier. Tap the holes in the extrusion ends and check whether they take M5 or M6 screws, since this depends on the extrusion maker. Take your time with the rails. This short video by 3D Distributed shows an easy way to align parallel rails. Reward yourself when the rails are in, you deserve it.

  4. Install the electronics. Check every connection against the wiring diagram, avoid shortcuts and use the right tools and parts. Connect the power cable last.

  5. Test and calibrate. Update the Duet WiFi to the latest firmware, copy the provided configuration to the micro SD card, insert it and power up. The Mini IR sensor should blink 4 times at power-up. Check the endstops before you move any axis. When you home the printer it should move left and then to the rear. If it doesn't, check the motor wiring and the configuration. Calibrate the Z height and check the temperature readings. Run a PID calibration for both the bed and the hotend. This step is essential, without it prints will fail. When everything looks right, load filament and print a calibration cube. Details are on the Calibrations page.

  6. Print and maintain. Grease the rails with a synthetic PTFE grease or sewing machine oil. Keep the rails clean and the belts tight. Clean the PEI plate with alcohol after every print. If you built the air scrubber, replace the HEPA filter when needed.

  7. Share your build. I would really appreciate an "I made one" photo. Knowing the project helped you build your own printer makes all the hours worth it.

  8. Remix and share. There are many ways to make this printer better, which is why the source files are included. Improve it and share your remixes with the community.

docs.title: BLV mgn12 mod
docs.text:
For Anet A8 / Prusa i3

This project turns the Anet A8 into a precise 3D printer, with MGN12 rails mounted on an aluminum extrusion frame. With small changes it is compatible with Pheneeny's AM8 mod. The result is a much more reliable, accurate and faster printer.

Download all files Thingiverse Remixes Facebook group

docs.title: Why
docs.text: Low and mid range printers usually move on linear bearings or Delrin wheels because they are cheaper than MGN rails, and the price is accuracy and reliability. MGN linear rails are stiffer, very precise and smooth. They allow faster printing without losing quality, and because the rails are fixed to the frame, they block unwanted motion from bent threaded rods or the other axes. That is why high-end printers use them. Affordable MGN rails on AliExpress made this upgrade possible.

docs.text:
Patience required

Mounting the MGN rails takes a lot of patience. They must be perfectly straight and aligned, and rushing this step causes problems later.

  • Source file. The STEP file is included in the project ZIP so the design can be improved. Please follow the license (Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial Share-Alike).
  • If you use the STEP file, mark your work as a remix.
  • A Simplify3D build plate is available for this project.

Note

You may need to re-center the bed coordinates in the Marlin configuration, or move the Z extrusion to center the hotbed.

Seeing community members share photos and remixes makes the long hours worth it. An "I made one" photo is always appreciated.

docs.title: Mod variations
docs.text:
1. Anet A8 converted to AM8 (original 440 mm height) with the BLV mgn12 mod. If you already own an AM8 and want to keep its height, use 350 mm rails instead of 400 mm.

  2. Anet A8 converted to AM8 with a taller 500 mm Z axis and the BLV mgn12 mod. Build the AM8 with these changes:

    • instead of 2 × 440 mm 2040 extrusions → 2 × 500 mm (or longer) 2040 extrusions
    • instead of 2 × 340 mm 2040 extrusions → 4 × 364 mm 2040 extrusions
    • longer 400 mm threaded rods

    Not all the AM8 parts are needed, see what to print. 3. Anet AM8 freestyle with the BLV mgn12 mod. The parts are modular and can be fitted as you like. For a custom size with a bigger bed or a taller Z axis, choose the extrusion lengths and attach the parts to them.

docs.title: Rail tips
docs.text:
I started with affordable MGN12H rails from AliExpress at about $18 each. After buying from four different sellers, I found the best value at the CNA Mechanical Parts Store. Their carriages slide smoothly straight out of the box, with no cleaning needed. For higher quality at a reasonable price, the HIWIN rail set is excellent.

Sellers to avoid

Avoid RDC Official Store and linkcnc Store on AliExpress. linkcnc sent me a used, damaged rail that was shorter than ordered and stayed stuck even after cleaning. RDC started shipping carriages that don't match the MGN standard.

Cleaning and lubrication. New rails usually feel rough because they are coated with a protective oil at the factory. Clean it off (several YouTube videos show how to clean the carriage with WD-40), then lubricate the rails and carriages with sewing machine oil or a PTFE silicone grease. These are miniature rails, so avoid thick grease. The goal is a smooth carriage without free play.

The video below shows the cleaning process well. Work over a container so you don't lose any steel balls. After reassembly there is room for one more ball, which is normal.

Tuning up cheap Chinese linear bearings

Mounting the rails takes patience. They must be perfectly straight and aligned, and rushing this step causes problems later.

Don't rely on the gravity test

Tilting a rail and watching the carriage slide down says nothing about its quality. A rail with too much free play passes easily and then fails every print quality test. The tolerance grade of the rail sets the friction of the carriage.
